items.note: canonical travel cliche; nothing is hidden in the internet age; top of every AI travel pattern list
items.example: This restaurant is a true hidden gem tucked away from the main street.

items.note: double-stacked travel cliche combining 'nestled' and 'in the heart of'; near-universal in AI travel openers
items.example: The boutique hotel is nestled in the heart of the old town.

items.note: 'nestled' is flagged across all AI travel catalogs; 'nestled among' is the second most common compound
items.example: The villa is nestled among olive trees with sweeping views.

items.note: companion cliche to 'nestled'; used for any elevated location in travel writing
items.example: The monastery is perched atop a rocky cliff overlooking the sea.

items.note: obligatory destination framing; appears in virtually every AI travel/review list
items.example: The rooftop bar is a must-visit if you're in the area.

items.note: same obligatory-framing pattern as must-visit; interchangeable in AI output
items.example: The waterfall is an absolute must-see attraction.

items.note: activity variant of the must-X pattern; third item in AI's must-X rotation
items.example: Taking a cooking class here is a must-do experience.

items.note: passive-voice variant of must-see; appears in same contexts
items.example: The sunset from the terrace is not to be missed.

items.note: canonical AI travel phrase; one of the most documented travel cliches across all sources
items.example: We found an off the beaten path village that wasn't in any guidebook.

items.note: variant of 'hidden gem'; implies exclusive knowledge the writer doesn't actually have
items.example: This little trattoria is the best-kept secret in the neighborhood.

items.note: most common sight descriptor in AI travel; no specifics about what makes the view notable
items.example: The hike rewards you with breathtaking views of the valley.

items.note: near-synonym of 'breathtaking views'; AI rotates between the two
items.example: The drive through the mountains offers stunning scenery at every turn.

items.note: culture descriptor AI applies to any destination; 'vibrant' is specifically flagged as a tourism-brochure tell; FP risk is higher in genuine local-color writing
items.example: Marrakech is known for its vibrant culture and colorful souks.

items.note: signal is when it appears alone with no dates, events, or names to back it up
items.example: The city has a rich history dating back thousands of years.

items.note: generic rural descriptor; AI's default adjective for any small European settlement
items.example: We stumbled upon a charming village with cobblestone streets.

items.note: adjective AI applies to any small town, shop, or cafe; overused as a filler descriptor
items.example: The quaint little cafe serves homemade pastries every morning.

items.note: urban descriptor pair; 'bustling' is flagged as a tourism-brochure AI tell in multiple sources
items.example: The market is surrounded by bustling streets full of vendors.

items.note: generic engagement imperative AI uses for any cultural or sensory experience
items.example: Immerse yourself in the local culture with a guided food tour.

items.note: generic discovery frame; filler that can precede any destination name
items.example: Discover the wonders of ancient Rome on a private walking tour.

items.note: universal-appeal filler that applies to any destination; signals absence of specific audience knowledge
items.example: Whether you love history or beaches, this city has something for everyone.

items.note: temporal-contrast formula AI uses to sound culturally observant; the slot filler varies but the structure is invariant
items.example: This district is where ancient tradition meets modern art.

items.note: unearned endorsement formula; AI's default closing for any positive review without specific reasons
items.example: I highly recommend this restaurant to anyone visiting the city.

items.note: classic pivot phrase at the end of a padded intro; documented in recipe blog and listicle research
items.example: Without further ado, here's my recipe for the perfect carbonara.

items.note: recipe and review filler that pairs any two attributes; 'blend' is a food metaphor misapplied universally
items.example: This dish is the perfect blend of sweet and savory flavors.

items.note: search-termination formula; signals AI's directive voice in guides and listicles
items.example: If you're looking for a family-friendly resort, look no further.

items.note: overused aspiration frame; FP risk is moderate since humans use it too, but it dominates AI travel output
items.example: A safari in the Serengeti is a true bucket list experience.

items.note: compound of 'bucket list'; more specific to AI travel writing than 'bucket list' alone
items.example: Santorini has long been a bucket list destination for honeymooners.

items.note: water descriptor appearing in virtually every AI beach/lake travel piece; 'crystal clear' is already in cliches.json as 'crystal clear' (without hyphen) - this compound is the travel-specific version
items.example: The island is famous for its crystal-clear waters and white sand.

items.note: alliterative landscape cliche; AI's default descriptor for any mountain range
items.example: The resort is surrounded by majestic mountains on three sides.

items.note: FP risk is high in isolation - legitimate phrase; signal is when used as a placeholder with no dish names, flavors, or specifics anywhere nearby
items.example: Be sure to sample the local cuisine during your visit.

items.note: value-affirmation with no comparative basis; confirmed in product review slop catalog
items.example: The tasting menu is expensive but worth every penny.

items.note: generic satisfaction formula appearing across AI reviews with no specifics about what the expectations were
items.example: The hotel exceeded my expectations in every way.

items.note: faked emotional reaction; asserts emotion without conveying it; AI review pattern
items.example: I was blown away by how good the pasta was.

items.note: unearned prediction common in recipe blog slop; 'you'll love this recipe' variant is documented
items.example: You'll love this easy weeknight pasta dish.

items.text: trust me, you won't be disappointed
items.note: false promise with no factual basis; documented in recipe blog quality/approval padding
items.example: Trust me, you won't be disappointed with this chocolate cake.

items.note: softening opener that delays the actual content; documented as recipe-blog good-news softener
items.example: The good news is this recipe only requires five ingredients.

items.text: what makes this recipe special is
items.note: self-congratulatory recipe setup that precedes a generic claim about the dish
items.example: What makes this recipe special is the way the spices come together.

items.note: generic occasion-stacking opener; signal is when followed by a list of 3+ unrelated occasions
items.example: This recipe is perfect for weeknight dinners, holidays, or meal prep.

items.text: even picky eaters will love it
items.note: audience-widening filler that broadens appeal without evidence; documented recipe slop
items.example: This mac and cheese is so good even picky eaters will love it.

items.text: my grandmother used to make this
items.note: synthetic nostalgia opener; AI has no grandmother; signal when there are no concrete details (no name, year, place)
items.example: My grandmother used to make this stew every Sunday in winter.

items.text: this dish brings back so many memories
items.note: unfounded emotional anchor in recipe intros; AI cannot have food memories
items.example: This lasagna brings back so many memories of family gatherings.

items.note: intensified variant of 'hidden gem'; factually false in the internet era
items.example: This stretch of coastline is an undiscovered paradise for surfers.

items.note: compressed variant of 'off the beaten path'; very common in AI travel recommendations
items.example: Head north to escape the crowds and find deserted beaches.

items.note: vague experience directive; AI travel writing staple that substitutes for specific descriptions
items.example: Grab a coffee and soak up the atmosphere of the old market square.

items.note: metaphorical engagement imperative in travel copy; applies to any street, neighborhood, or market
items.example: Lose yourself in the winding alleys of the medina.

items.note: hyperbolic experience frame; 'magic' as a placeholder noun signals tourism-brochure AI output
items.example: Experience the magic of Kyoto during cherry blossom season.

items.note: empty paradox framing applied to any city; signals no specific knowledge of the destination
items.example: Istanbul is truly a city of contrasts, where east meets west.

items.note: jewel-descriptor superlative applied to any region or country; formulaic travel praise
items.example: Known as the pearl of the Indian Ocean, this island draws millions of visitors.

items.note: double AI tell: 'rich' (vague) + 'tapestry' (confirmed 227x overuse noun); compound is very low FP risk
items.example: The country offers a rich cultural tapestry woven over centuries.

items.note: FP risk is high in isolation; signal is when used as the primary location descriptor with no additional specifics; often combined with 'nestled'
items.example: The restaurant is located in the heart of the historic district.

items.note: occasion-stacking filler in recipe copy; often appears in a triple with holidays and meal prep
items.example: This quick pasta dish is great for weeknight dinners when time is short.

items.note: superlative assertion without test or comparison; 'hands-down' compound is an AI emphasis tick
items.example: This is hands-down the best chocolate chip cookie recipe you'll ever try.

items.note: avoids specifics about what the results are; AI filler to end a section without committing to evidence
items.example: Use the freshest ingredients and the results speak for themselves.

items.note: transformation formula applied to reviews; AI cannot transform its behavior through product use
items.example: This cast iron skillet completely transformed how I cook at home.

items.text: after using this for a few weeks
items.note: vague duration in review copy; AI cannot test products; the vagueness is the signal
items.example: After using this for a few weeks, I can say it holds up well.

items.note: pseudo-authoritative review closer; part of the product review conclusion scaffolding cluster
items.example: Final verdict: a solid choice for anyone looking to upgrade their kitchen.

items.note: fake-balance setup that precedes a trivial or token flaw; structural review slop
items.example: No product is perfect, but the minor size issue doesn't diminish the value.

items.text: whether you're a food lover or
items.note: 'whether you're X or Y' template applied to travel/food; false inclusivity scaffold
items.example: Whether you're a food lover or a history buff, this city won't disappoint.

items.note: 'journey' applied to food; combines two AI slop words into a food-writing cliche
items.example: Dining here is a culinary journey through the flavors of southern Italy.

items.note: portmanteau travel-food cliche; 'foodie' as an adjective + 'paradise' as a superlative noun
items.example: Barcelona is a foodie paradise with tapas bars on every corner.

items.note: food descriptor AI applies without specifying what the flavors are; 'tantalizing' is a tourism-brochure intensifier
items.example: The menu is packed with tantalizing flavors from around the world.

items.note: recipe and restaurant review filler; 'bursting with' is AI's default intensifier for food descriptions
items.example: Every bite is bursting with flavor thanks to the slow-roasted spices.

items.note: texture/quality descriptor used in recipe and review copy without specifying the technique; cliche even in human writing but overrepresented in AI output
items.example: The braised short rib is melt-in-your-mouth tender after six hours of cooking.

items.note: synesthetic cliche applied to any dining or travel experience; implies all five senses without describing any
items.example: Walking through the spice market is a feast for the senses.

items.note: plural variant of 'hidden gem'; used in listicle and guide contexts for any local recommendation
items.example: Skip the tourist traps and seek out the local gems instead.

items.note: visual-superlative compound AI applies to any scenic location or plated dish
items.example: The village square is absolutely picture-perfect at golden hour.

items.note: variant of 'off the beaten path'; AI rotates between these to avoid self-repetition
items.example: The waterfalls are off the tourist trail and worth the extra hike.

items.note: intensified variant of 'hidden gem' used when the place is no longer positioned as hidden
items.example: This neighborhood bistro is a true gem of the local dining scene.

items.note: temporal-immersion cliche for historic destinations or traditional restaurants
items.example: Walking through the old city feels like stepping back in time.

items.note: 'world-class' is in corporate-speak.json as a word; this phrase is the travel/review-specific compound form
items.example: The resort offers world-class dining with panoramic ocean views.

items.note: itinerary-insertion formula; variant of must-visit applied to planning contexts
items.example: The archaeological museum is a must for any itinerary in Athens.

items.note: superlative view descriptor with no comparative basis; AI's alternative to 'breathtaking'
items.example: The rooftop terrace offers unparalleled views of the city skyline.

items.note: directive opener in restaurant reviews; signals AI's attempt to sound casual and knowing
items.example: Come hungry - the portions here are enormous.

items.note: hospitality-directive cliche in restaurant reviews; appears formulaically after praising mains
items.example: The mains are excellent, but be sure to leave room for dessert.

items.note: catch-all review closer; variant of 'has something for everyone'; applied to any positively reviewed venue
items.example: Great food, reasonable prices, friendly staff - this place has it all.

items.note: unearned guarantee formula in review sign-offs; AI's default closing endorsement
items.example: Book the sunset cruise - you won't regret it.
